expl.summary: Every jet is placed on 16 scales, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables (for the mass observables the if-statements could also use offered candidate thresholds at 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 times the W, Z, H and top masses; in this smaller formula the thresholds are rounded to three significant digits, and 91.2 GeV in neuron 7, 86.4 GeV in neuron 5 and 173 GeV in neuron 13 match such offered values), and each class score adds some scales and subtracts others; the formula classifies 81.1% of validation jets correctly. The g score rests mainly on particle multiplicity (neuron 1: many particles with pT spread over them, +47%, and the neuron whose freezing costs the most accuracy, 12.0 points), from which the q score subtracts (-22%); the two light-parton scores are separated from the heavier jets by subtracting a scale that is off for jets lighter than about 86 GeV and follows low D2 and τ21 (neuron 4, -32% of the q score, -16% of the g score) and by adding a scale that is largest for light jets with high τ21 and D2 (neuron 9, +24% of the q score, +14% of the g score). The W and Z scores both subtract the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, -25% and -26%) and add a scale for few particles and jet mass between about 74 and 158 GeV (neuron 5, +15% and +18%). W and Z are split by jet mass: a scale peaking at a jet mass near 78 GeV (neuron 0) raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-20%), a compact scale for jets whose 50 hardest particles are lighter than 94.7 GeV (neuron 11) raises the W score (+11%), while a mass band of about 91-102 GeV with almost all pT inside ΔR < 0.3 (neuron 7) raises the Z score (+8%) and lowers the W score (-6%), and a scale for jets heavier than about 83-92 GeV (neuron 14) lowers the W score (-10%). The t score subtracts a total-pT scale that is switched off for heavy jets (neuron 13, -36%) and adds broad angular spread (neuron 10: large girth, LHA and τ1, +29%).

0.measures: Its strongest term pushes it down as the jet mass rises above 78.3 GeV; it is pushed down further above 93.8 GeV and, weakly, for jets lighter than 99.1 GeV (more the lighter the jet), and partly restored when the 50 hardest particles have mass above 82.0 GeV. So it rises slowly with mass up to 78.3 GeV and falls steeply above; most heavy jets are at zero. It is pushed up for small mass/pT (mass/pT squared < 0.00766), for pT of the 50 hardest particles below 1160 GeV and for fewer than 15.3 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4, and pushed down for very small e2_sq (< 0.00614). Over all jets it falls with mass (rank correlation -0.661) and with mass/pT, width and girth2 (-0.638 each), because the heaviest jets sit at zero. W jets sit highest (1.62), then quarks (0.68), gluons (0.36) and Z jets (0.28), with tops lowest (0.09). It is zero for 1.5% of W jets, 20.3% of quarks, 33.4% of Z jets, 48.0% of gluons and 90.9% of tops.
0.role: It raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-20%), so it separates jets near 78 GeV from heavier ones. It hardly enters the t score (+2%) and does not enter the g or q scores. Freezing it costs 1.67 accuracy points.

1.title: many particles, pT spread over many of them
1.measures: It follows the number of particles (rank correlation 0.67) and the number of particles above 1 GeV (0.65), and falls with the pT share of the 40 hardest particles (-0.626). Its strongest term pushes it down when the softest real particle has pT < 2.27 GeV (this pT is 0 when that particle is among the 15 hardest), largely offset below 1.5 GeV by a term of opposite sign. It is pushed up for high total pT (log of total pT > 6.91 and > 6.89, pulled back above 6.97), for pT entropy > 2.0, for τ1 < 0.196 and for more than 38.4 particles, and pushed down when the pT of the 50 hardest particles exceeds 953 GeV, when these particles carry more than 96% of the pT and when more than 10.4 particles are needed for 90% of the pT. Gluons sit far highest (5.83), then tops (2.92), quarks (2.17), Z (1.84) and W jets (1.70). It is almost never zero (0.1% of gluons, 0.7% of tops, 4.6% of Z, 6.6% of W and 8.2% of quarks).
1.role: It raises the g score, where it is the largest input (+47%), and lowers the q score (-22%), so it separates gluons from quarks by multiplicity. It does not enter the W, Z or t scores. Freezing it costs 12.0 accuracy points, the most of any neuron.

2.title: high total jet pT with a compact core of the 15 hardest particles
2.measures: It is a single product of two if-statements: it is essentially zero unless the log of the total pT exceeds 6.91 and the pT-weighted mean ΔR² of the 15 hardest particles is below 0.0272, and it grows with both margins. It follows the log of the total pT and the total pT (rank correlation 0.858 each) and the pT of the 50 hardest particles (0.856). Gluons sit highest (0.59), then W (0.20), Z (0.18) and quarks (0.18), with tops lowest (0.05); it is zero for 28.6% of gluons, 30.4% of W, 32.2% of Z, 50.9% of quarks and 82.0% of tops.
2.role: It lowers the Z score slightly (-2%) and hardly enters the q score (+1%); it does not enter the g, W or t scores. Its effect on the classification is small (freezing it changes accuracy by 0.008 points).

3.title: few particles, thin jet (small λ2, τ3, τ4)
3.measures: It falls with the smaller eigenvalue λ2 of the pT-weighted (Δη, Δφ) tensor (rank correlation -0.806), the number of particles (-0.785), τ4 (-0.783) and τ3 (-0.766). Its strongest terms push it up for fewer than 46.1 particles and for λ2 < 0.000625, and down when the 50 hardest particles have mass < 69.2 GeV (more the lighter). It is also pushed up when fewer than 7.15 particles lie at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 and the 50 hardest particles carry more than 98% of the pT (a product of the two), for girth2 of the 40 hardest particles < 0.00669, and when fewer than 11.2 particles lie at 0.1 ≤ ΔR < 0.2 with more than 93.4% of the pT within ΔR < 0.2; it is pushed down for τ21 < 0.375 and for τ21 < 0.406 combined with λ1 > 0.00572. W jets sit highest (0.69), then quarks (0.61) and Z jets (0.44), with gluons (0.15) and tops (0.04) low; it is zero for 5.3% of W jets, 20.8% of Z, 21.2% of quarks, 50.2% of gluons and 89.0% of tops.
3.role: It raises the W score (+4%) and the Z score (+4%) and lowers the g score (-8%), where gluons, with more particles, sit low. It does not enter the q or t scores.

4.title: off for jets lighter than about 86 GeV, low D2 and τ21
4.measures: Built mainly from jet-mass steps: pushed down for jets lighter than 86.2 GeV (its strongest term) and, more steeply, lighter than 78.4 GeV, pushed up for mass < 119 GeV (most for jets just above 86.2 GeV), pushed down when the 40 hardest particles have mass < 166 GeV and up again when their mass is < 67.5 GeV. So it is off for most light jets and on for most jets heavier than about 86 GeV. It is also pushed up for e2_sq > 0.0103, for fewer than 24.2 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 and for more than 99.7% of the pT within ΔR < 0.3, and pushed down for more than 23.1 particles, for girth2 of the 15 hardest particles > 0.00752 and for λ1 > 0.00794. It falls with D2 (β = 2) (rank correlation -0.701), D2 (-0.693), τ21 (β = 2) (-0.676) and N2 (-0.66) and rises with the mass of the 10 hardest particles (0.651). Z jets sit highest (1.43), then W (1.14) and tops (0.73), with gluons (0.17) and quarks (0.10) low; it is zero for 82.7% of quarks and 64.7% of gluons, but only for 8.6-11.7% of Z, top and W jets.
4.role: It lowers the q score, where it is the largest input (-32%), and the g score (-16%), and raises the W score (+6%) and the t score (+3%). It does not enter the Z score.

5.title: few particles, jet mass between about 74 and 158 GeV
5.measures: Many of its terms are on total pT and partly cancel: pushed up for pT of the 50 hardest particles > 943 GeV and total pT > 908 GeV, pushed down for log of total pT > 6.91 and total pT > 990 GeV. On mass it is pushed up above 73.6 GeV and for groomed (soft-drop) mass above 72.1 GeV, and pushed down above 92.4 GeV, for groomed mass above 86.4 GeV (a value that matches one of the offered candidate thresholds, half the top mass), for mass/pT > 0.0781 and, steeply, when the 50 hardest particles have mass above 158 GeV. It is pushed up for max ΔR < 0.459, for fewer than 47.5 particles and for fewer than 12.4 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4. It falls with the number of particles (rank correlation -0.622), the number at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (-0.62) and λ2 (-0.604), and rises with the pT share of the 30 hardest particles (0.578). Z jets sit highest (1.67), then W (1.46) and quarks (1.41), with gluons (0.53) and tops (0.29) low; it is zero for 0.5% of Z, 0.7% of W, 7.4% of quarks, 27.1% of gluons and 65.9% of tops.
5.role: It raises the Z score (+18%) and the W score (+15%) and lowers the t score (-13%) and the g score (-9%). It does not enter the q score.

6.title: high D2 and τ21, small e2, jet mass outside about 73-102 GeV
6.measures: Its two strongest terms are on jet mass: pushed down for jets lighter than 102 GeV, with the push growing down to 93.9 GeV and held nearly constant below, because a second term pushes it up for mass < 93.9 GeV with an almost equal slope. It is pushed back up for light jets when the 50 hardest particles have mass < 73.3 GeV, and for girth2 of the 20 hardest particles > 0.00733; it is pushed down for mass/pT > 0.121, for e2 > 0.0294 and when girth2 of the 20 hardest particles > 0.0035 and C2 (β = 2) > 0.00379 together. It rises with D2 (β = 2) (rank correlation 0.506), τ21 (β = 2) (0.493), D2 and the number of branches removed by soft drop (0.481 each), and falls with e2 (-0.493). Quarks sit highest (1.20), then gluons (0.80) and tops (0.40); W and Z jets sit at 0.10 and are zero for 86.5% and 84.4% of them (gluons 12.5%, quarks 8.5%, tops 50.4%).
6.role: It lowers the Z score (-12%) and raises the q score (+5%) and the g score (+2%). It hardly enters the W score (+1%) and does not enter the t score.

7.title: jet mass 91-102 GeV with almost all pT within ΔR < 0.3
7.measures: Built from products of a jet-mass condition (mass < 91.0, 91.2, 93.2, 102, 82.3, 101 or 91.5 GeV) with the pT share within ΔR < 0.3 of the axis (above 0.964, 0.978 or 0.998). Terms with neighbouring mass thresholds enter with opposite signs (mass < 102 with share > 0.978 pushes up, mass < 91.0 with share > 0.978 pushes down; mass < 91.2 with share > 0.964 pushes up, mass < 93.2 with share > 0.964 pushes down), so the neuron responds mainly to jets with mass between about 91 and 102 GeV that have almost all their pT within ΔR < 0.3. The threshold 91.2 GeV matches the offered Z-mass candidate threshold. It is also pushed down for τ1 < 0.107 and for groomed (soft-drop) mass < 87.2 GeV, and up for groomed mass < 69.8 GeV. It falls with the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlation -0.492) and rises with the pT share within ΔR < 0.3 (0.466). Z jets sit far highest (1.48); quarks (0.14), W (0.13), gluons (0.08) and tops (0.06) are near zero. It is zero for 12.3% of Z jets, but for 46.3% of quarks, 54.3% of W, 72.9% of gluons and 84.3% of tops.
7.role: It raises the Z score (+8%) and lowers the W score (-6%) and the t score (-3%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

8.title: wide, massive jet (large width, girth2, mass/pT)
8.measures: It rises with mass/pT, width and girth2 (rank correlation 0.718 each) and e2_sq (0.717). Its strongest term pushes it up as the jet mass rises above 71.1 GeV, with smaller terms pulling it back above 103 and 127 GeV; it is pushed down for narrow jets (width < 0.00987) and when the 50 hardest particles carry more than 97.2% of the pT, and on girth2 of the 20 hardest particles it is pushed down above 0.0059 and up above 0.00788. It is pushed up when mass/pT > 0.0785 with total pT < 1100 GeV and for total pT < 1030 GeV, and pushed down for fewer than 17.9 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4. Tops sit far highest (3.46), then gluons (1.41) and quarks (0.58), with Z (0.28) and W jets (0.05) lowest; it is zero for 3.8% of tops, 32.7% of gluons, 42.6% of Z, 71.0% of quarks and 88.8% of W jets.
8.role: It lowers the Z score (-26%) and the W score (-25%), where it is the largest input of both, and raises the t score (+6%). It hardly enters the g or q scores (+1% each).

9.title: light jets (mass below about 85 GeV), high τ21 and D2
9.measures: Almost entirely a function of jet mass. Two large terms nearly cancel: it is pushed up for mass < 178 GeV (its strongest term) and down for mass < 147 GeV, so jets heavier than 178 GeV get nothing from them, jets of 147-178 GeV get a small bump, and below 147 GeV the value falls slowly as the mass decreases; it is then pushed up steeply for mass < 85.5 GeV, with most of that slope taken back below 62.9 GeV. The net result is largest for light jets. Smaller terms push it up for girth2 of the 40 hardest particles < 0.00617 and for girth > 0.0976, and down when the 40 hardest particles carry more than 95.4% of the pT. It rises with τ21 (β = 2) (rank correlation 0.679), D2 (β = 2) (0.661), τ21 (0.653) and planar flow (0.63) and falls with eccentricity (-0.63). Quarks sit highest (2.35), then gluons (1.60) and tops (0.64), with W (0.31) and Z jets (0.21) low; it is zero for 89.4% of Z, 67.5% of W, 23.9% of tops, 15.6% of gluons and 10.1% of quarks.
9.role: It raises the q score (+24%) and the g score (+14%) and lowers the W score (-5%). It does not enter the Z or t scores.

10.title: broad angular spread (large girth, LHA, τ1)
10.measures: It rises with LHA (rank correlation 0.753), τ1 (0.751) and girth (0.75) and falls with the pT share within ΔR < 0.05 (-0.727). Its strongest term pushes it up for jets lighter than 87.9 GeV, offset by a term pushing it down below 99.6 GeV; it is also pushed down above 145 GeV and slightly up above 78.8 GeV. It is pushed down when the harder of two subjets has mass < 65.0 GeV, for τ1 < 0.047 and for girth2 of the 20 hardest particles < 0.00533, and pushed up for e2 > 0.0128, D2 < 3.04, pT of the 15 hardest particles < 941 GeV and τ2 < 0.0485. Tops sit highest (2.40), then Z (1.01), W (0.99), gluons (0.88) and quarks (0.57); it is zero for 3.5% of tops, 12.9% of Z, 13.8% of W, 33.3% of gluons and 56.3% of quarks.
10.role: It raises the t score (+29%), its second-largest input. It hardly enters the g and q scores (-0.5% and -0.8%) and does not enter the W or Z scores. Freezing it costs 2.32 accuracy points, the second-largest loss after neuron 1.

11.title: mass of the 50 hardest particles below 94.7 GeV, compact, few particles
11.measures: Its strongest term pushes it up as the mass of the 50 hardest particles falls below 94.7 GeV, and a term of nearly equal slope pushes it down below 80.9 GeV, so it rises from 94.7 to 80.9 GeV and stays about level for lighter jets. It is pushed down for the narrowest jets (girth2 of the 30 hardest particles < 0.00666) and up for e2 < 0.0266, for fewer than 7.5 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4, for fewer than 16.7 particles at 0.1 ≤ ΔR < 0.2 and when more than 99% of the pT is within ΔR < 0.3. It falls with λ2 (rank correlation -0.737), the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (-0.705), τ4 (-0.69) and the number of particles (-0.683). W jets sit highest (1.52), then Z (0.96) and quarks (0.77), with gluons (0.40) and tops (0.13) low; it is zero for 2.1% of W, 6.6% of Z, 14.6% of quarks, 34.3% of gluons and 77.7% of tops.
11.role: It raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the q score (-8%). It does not enter the g, Z or t scores.

12.title: jet mass below 83.4 GeV, rising as the mass falls to about 60 GeV
12.measures: Its strongest term pushes it up as the jet mass falls below 83.4 GeV; below 59.7 GeV a second term takes most of this slope back, so it rises from 83.4 down to about 60 GeV and changes little for lighter jets. It is pulled down for a very compact core (girth2 of the 15 hardest particles < 0.00586), for mass < 90.0 GeV combined with a pT share within ΔR < 0.3 below 0.999, and slightly for log of total pT < 6.85 combined with λ2 < 0.0036. It falls with mass (rank correlation -0.632), the mass of the 50 hardest particles (-0.623) and mass/pT and width (-0.616 each). Quarks sit highest (1.42), then gluons (0.64) and W jets (0.27), with Z (0.11) and tops (0.08) low; it is zero for 22.7% of quarks, 40.5% of W, 51.9% of gluons, 77.1% of tops and 92.6% of Z jets.
12.role: It raises the q score (+7%), the Z score (+4%) and the g score (+3%), and lowers the W score (-5%) and the t score (-5%).

13.title: total jet pT, switched off for heavy jets
13.measures: It rises with the log of the total pT and the total pT (rank correlation 0.641 each) and the pT of the 50 hardest particles (0.621). Its strongest term pushes it down for log of total pT < 6.92; it is pushed up for jet mass above 63.1 GeV and for pT of the 40 hardest particles < 1020 GeV, and pushed down for total pT < 1090 GeV combined with τ21 (β = 2) < 1.0. Heavy jets are pushed down by several terms: mass above 173 GeV together with a pT share of the fifth-softest real particle above 0.000296 (a steep product; 173 GeV matches the offered top-mass candidate threshold), mass above 142 GeV with D2 > 0.0302, mass above 101 GeV and above 161 GeV, partly offset by mass above 169 GeV with D2 > 0.281. Z jets sit highest (2.03), then W (1.86), gluons (1.70) and quarks (1.53); tops sit lowest (0.68) and are zero for 42.7% of them (Z 0.4%, W 0.5%, quarks 8.6%, gluons 15.1%).
13.role: It lowers the t score, where it is the largest input (-36%). It does not enter the g, q, W or Z scores.

14.title: jet mass above about 83-92 GeV, mass/pT below 0.144
14.measures: Its strongest terms push it down for jets lighter than 92.0 GeV and, more steeply, lighter than 82.8 GeV, partly restored when the 50 hardest particles have mass < 78.4 GeV; on mass/pT it is pushed up below 0.144 and down when mass/pT < 0.0905 coincides with more than 91.4% of the pT within ΔR < 0.2. It is pushed down for the narrowest jets (girth2 of the 30 hardest particles < 0.00262) and up when more than 99.3% of the pT is within ΔR < 0.3 and for e2 < 0.0302. It rises weakly with mass (rank correlation 0.387) and the mass of the 50 hardest particles (0.379). Z jets sit far highest (0.89); gluons (0.22), tops (0.20), quarks (0.08) and W jets (0.04) are near zero. It is zero for 14.6% of Z jets, 60.3% of tops, 69.1% of gluons, 86.4% of W and 87.7% of quarks.
14.role: It lowers the W score (-10%), separating Z jets, heavier than the 82.8-92.0 GeV thresholds, from W jets. It does not enter the g, q, Z or t scores.

15.title: groomed mass below 73.6 GeV, low total pT, small LHA and girth
15.measures: Its strongest terms push it up as the groomed (soft-drop) mass falls below 73.6 GeV, with most of that slope taken back below 44.2 GeV, and push it up for log of total pT < 7.03. It is pushed down when more than 85.7% of the pT is within ΔR < 0.2 and when more than 98.9% is within ΔR < 0.3, for pT of the 40 hardest particles < 1020 GeV, for e2 > 0.0294 and for τ1 < 0.0678; it is pushed up for λ2 < 0.00181 and for fewer than 13.6 particles at 0.1 ≤ ΔR < 0.2. It falls with the pT share at 0.1 ≤ ΔR < 0.2 (rank correlation -0.589), LHA (-0.555), τ1, groomed mass and girth (-0.543 each), and rises with the pT share within ΔR < 0.05 (0.566). Quarks sit highest (0.59), then W (0.44), Z (0.44) and gluons (0.34), with tops lowest (0.11); it is zero for 17.7% of quarks, 37.1% of W, 41.0% of gluons, 57.7% of Z and 82.0% of tops.
15.role: It raises the Z score (+5%) and lowers the t score (-4%). It hardly enters the W score (-2%) and does not enter the g or q scores.

g.title: gluon: many particles, not two-prong
g.measures: High for jets with many particles and no two-prong structure: it rises with N2 (rank correlation 0.694), τ21 (β = 2) (0.673) and planar flow (0.65) and falls with eccentricity (-0.65). It averages 3.27 for g jets, 1.04 for q and 0.48 for t, and is negative for W (-1.76) and Z (-1.88) (AUC 0.93 for gluons against the rest).
g.built_from: Mostly adds multiplicity (neuron 1, +47%) and the light-jet scale with high τ21 (neuron 9, +14%); subtracts the low-D2 scale that is off for light jets (neuron 4, -16%), the few-particles moderate-mass scale (neuron 5, -9%) and the thin few-particle scale (neuron 3, -8%); adds a little of neurons 12 (+3%) and 6 (+2%).

q.title: light quark: high D2 and τ21, fewer particles
q.measures: High for jets with high D2 and τ21 (rank correlations 0.705 with D2 for β = 2, 0.693 with τ21 for β = 2, 0.66 with D2). It averages 2.75 for q jets and 1.37 for g (gluons are its main confusion), 0.51 for t, and is negative for W (-0.25) and Z (-0.55) (AUC 0.89).
q.built_from: Subtracts the low-D2 scale that is off for light jets (neuron 4, -32%, its largest input) and multiplicity (neuron 1, -22%), and the compact scale for jets whose 50 hardest particles are lighter than 94.7 GeV (neuron 11, -8%); adds the light-jet scale with high τ21 (neuron 9, +24%), the below-83.4-GeV mass scale (neuron 12, +7%) and a little of neuron 6 (+5%).

W.title: W: compact jet, mass near 78 GeV
W.measures: High for compact jets with few particles and a mass near 78 GeV; over all jets it falls with mass (rank correlation -0.653) and with mass/pT, width and girth2 (-0.649 each), since massive wide jets are pushed far down. It averages 3.32 for W jets and 0.33 for q, is near zero for Z (-0.04), and negative for g (-1.18) and t (-2.83) (AUC 0.97).
W.built_from: Subtracts the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, -25%, its largest input); adds the few-particles moderate-mass scale (neuron 5, +15%), the mass-peak scale near 78 GeV (neuron 0, +11%) and the compact scale below 94.7 GeV (neuron 11, +11%), plus neurons 4 (+6%) and 3 (+4%); subtracts the scale for jets heavier than about 83-92 GeV (neuron 14, -10%), the 91-102 GeV band (neuron 7, -6%) and a little of neurons 9 and 12 (-5% each).

Z.title: Z: compact jet with few particles, heavier than 78 GeV
Z.measures: High for jets with few particles and small λ2, τ3 and τ4 (rank correlations -0.604 with λ2, -0.603 with τ4 and with the number of particles, -0.59 with τ3). It averages 3.13 for Z jets, 0.41 for q and 0.30 for W, and is negative for g (-0.94) and t (-2.43) (AUC 0.96).
Z.built_from: Subtracts the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, -26%) and the mass-peak scale near 78 GeV (neuron 0, -20%), which separates it from W jets, and the high-D2 scale (neuron 6, -12%); adds the few-particles moderate-mass scale (neuron 5, +18%), the 91-102 GeV band (neuron 7, +8%), the groomed-mass scale (neuron 15, +5%) and a little of neurons 3 and 12 (+4% each); subtracts a little of neuron 2 (-2%).

t.title: top: broad, massive jet
t.measures: High for broad jets: it rises with τ1 and girth (rank correlation 0.792 each), LHA (0.785), girth2 of the 5 hardest particles (0.743) and mass/pT (0.738). It averages 3.17 for t jets and is negative for all others: g (-0.15), W (-0.49), Z (-1.11) and q (-1.27) (AUC 0.96).
t.built_from: Subtracts the total-pT scale that is switched off for heavy jets (neuron 13, -36%, its largest input) and adds broad angular spread (neuron 10, +29%); subtracts the few-particles moderate-mass scale (neuron 5, -13%) and a little of neurons 12 (-5%), 15 (-4%) and 7 (-3%); adds a little of the wide, massive-jet scale (neuron 8, +6%) and of neuron 4 (+3%).

0.name: jets of about 79 GeV, narrow, pT at ΔR 0.05-0.1
0.jets: Mostly W (71%) with g 9%, t 7%, q 6%, Z 6%; 24.4% of all jets. Mean mass 79.2 GeV, width 0.0061, total pT 1021 GeV (all jets: 89.9 GeV, 0.0093, 1044 GeV); leading particle 240.81 GeV; 35% of the pT lies at ΔR 0.05-0.1 from the axis (all jets: 27%).
0.why: mass_over_sum_pt_sq < 0.00766 passes for 97% and adds +0.819; n_dr_0p2_0p4 < 15.3 passes for 95% and adds +0.501; sum_pt_top50 < 1.16e+03 passes for 98% and adds +0.434; z_dr_0p2_0p4 < 0.0913 passes for 98% and adds -0.338. Of the neuron's main terms, mass_top50 > 82 passes for only 16% here. The mass sits just above 78.3 GeV, so the steep step above it takes little (it passes for 73%), and the small-mass/pT term is the main addition. The neuron averages 1.454 and is on for 94%, adding +1.091 to the W score, -2.0 to the Z score, +0.182 to the t score; the formula calls them W (right for 82%).

1.name: jets of about 91 GeV, pT at ΔR 0.05-0.1
1.jets: Mostly Z (77%) with g 9%, t 8%, q 4%; 21.8% of all jets. Mean mass 91.2 GeV, width 0.0079, total pT 1037 GeV (all jets: 89.9 GeV, 0.0093, 1044 GeV); leading particle 240.27 GeV; 41% of the pT lies at ΔR 0.05-0.1 from the axis (all jets: 27%).
1.why: mass > 78.3 always passes and adds -2.012; n_dr_0p2_0p4 < 15.3 passes for 93% and adds +0.468; sum_pt_top50 < 1.16e+03 passes for 95% and adds +0.4; mass_top50 > 82 passes for 98% and adds +0.391. At this mass the step above 78.3 GeV takes much more (-2.012) than for the 79 GeV group, and mass_top50 > 82 (+0.391) gives back only a small part. The neuron averages 0.148 and is on for 50%, adding +0.111 to the W score, -0.203 to the Z score, +0.018 to the t score; the formula calls them Z (right for 88%).

2.name: light pencil-thin jets (35 GeV), pT within ΔR 0.025
2.jets: Mostly q (63%) with g 26%, W 5%, Z 5%; 17.5% of all jets. Mean mass 34.7 GeV, width 0.0011, total pT 1064 GeV (all jets: 89.9 GeV, 0.0093, 1044 GeV); leading particle 326.79 GeV; 87% of the pT lies at ΔR 0-0.025 from the axis (all jets: 29%).
2.why: mass_over_sum_pt_sq < 0.00766 always passes and adds +3.27; e2_sq < 0.00614 always passes and adds -1.578; mass < 99.1 always passes and adds -1.038; tau1 < 0.0699 always passes and adds -0.933. Of the neuron's main terms, mass > 78.3 never passes and mass_top50 > 82 never passes here. The small-mass/pT term (+3.27) outweighs the penalties for light mass (mass < 99.1), small e2_sq and small τ1. The neuron averages 0.682 and is on for 96%, adding +0.512 to the W score, -0.938 to the Z score, +0.085 to the t score; the formula calls them q (right for 78%).

3.name: light narrow jets of about 62 GeV
3.jets: Mostly g (47%) with q 32%, W 12%, Z 6%; 11.3% of all jets. Mean mass 61.7 GeV, width 0.0033, total pT 1077 GeV (all jets: 89.9 GeV, 0.0093, 1044 GeV); leading particle 252.73 GeV; 60% of the pT lies at ΔR 0-0.025 from the axis (all jets: 29%).
3.why: mass_over_sum_pt_sq < 0.00766 always passes and adds +2.166; e2_sq < 0.00614 always passes and adds -0.883; mass < 99.1 always passes and adds -0.603; tau1 < 0.0699 passes for 97% and adds -0.492.
